source_basis: Statista Consumer Market Outlook, Game Consoles - South Africa. 142,830 units at $395.30. VALIDATED: 2023 volume 140,620 vs our customs-tonnage estimate of 110,314-172,016 (midpoint 140,230) - 0.3% apart.
Statista, Game Consoles - Egypt. 34,640 units at $370.10. VALIDATED: matches the Comtrade MIRROR ($12.89m) to 0.5%, confirming Egypt's own declaration ($1.95m) understates by 6.6x.
Statista, Game Consoles - Nigeria. LOW retained at the Comtrade mirror ($1.44m) because Statista's Nigeria model is doubtful - see the users-per-console check below.
Statista Advertising & Media Outlook, Console Games - South Africa. LOW/HIGH span the 11-country comparator content-to-hardware band applied to validated hardware (1.00x to 1.97x).
Statista, Console Games - Egypt. Ratio to hardware 1.90 - almost exactly the comparator median of 1.97.
Statista, Console Games - Nigeria. LOW is the comparator median applied to the Comtrade-mirror hardware instead, for consistency with the low hardware case.

Statista brand shares 2022: PlayStation 66%, Xbox 21%, Other 13%. SUPERSEDES our earlier 41-56% assumption - our entire range sat BELOW the true figure. StatCounter's 41% measured web traffic, not ownership.
Statista brand shares 2022: PlayStation 64%, Xbox 22%, Nintendo 9%, Other 5%.
Statista brand shares 2022: PlayStation 47%, Xbox 25%, Nintendo 23%, Other 5%. Notably lower than SA/Egypt.
Roughly 30% on third-party digital titles, far more on first-party. Blended. NOT applied to hardware, where Sony is the seller.

UN Comtrade HS 950450, flow=Imports, partner=World, 2024. Sum of the 25 African reporters excluding South Africa, Egypt, Nigeria and Tunisia. Largest components: Morocco $4.51m, Mauritius $2.15m, Namibia $1.42m, Tanzania $0.89m, Kenya $0.86m, Angola $0.69m.

Tunisia's Comtrade figure is $33.17m, but it is UNSD-ESTIMATED (legacyEstimationFlag 6), not reported, and implies $2.654 per capita against South Africa's $0.740 - 3.6x the richest, most console-penetrated market on the continent. Replaced with a cap at South Africa's own per-capita rate x 12.5m people. Generous: Tunisian GDP per capita is ~2/3 of South Africa's.

Calibrated on the one African country where the customs declaration is credible: Statista's South Africa retail hardware ($56.46m) divided by South Africa's declared 2024 CIF imports ($46.74m). Covers duty, distribution and retail margin, net of the accessory content of the HS line.

THE SINGLE BIGGEST LEVER IN THIS LINE. South Africa needs no uplift (its mirror is lower than its own declaration). Egypt's mirror is 18.4x its declaration and Nigeria's 9.6x, but both are countries with known customs-reporting failure. Morocco, Kenya, Tanzania and Ghana report plausibly. Base 1.8x is a judgement between those poles.

26 of 54 African countries returned no 2024 data at all, including DR Congo, Ethiopia and Sudan - roughly 360m people. Valued at Kenya's declared rate of $0.016 per capita (=$5.8m) for the base, halved for LOW and ~2.8x for HIGH.

Comparator band from 11 countries: 1.23-5.33, median 1.97. LOW is the band floor, BASE the median, HIGH truncated at 3.00 rather than the 5.33 maximum, since the top of that band belongs to mature digital-first markets.
Statista's own Africa-wide console content ($378.56m) less the three case-study countries ($141.05m). Used only as a hard ceiling on the HIGH case, never as an estimate.
Between Nigeria's measured 47% and South Africa's 66%. North African markets (Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia) skew strongly to PlayStation; sub-Saharan markets outside South Africa skew less so.

SECOND-HAND DEDUCTION. HS 950450 does not distinguish new from used, and a second-hand console generates NO Sony hardware revenue - that sale was booked years earlier in the exporting market. Floor evidence: 12 of 21 African reporters declare BELOW the $40-150/kg boxed-console band (Tanzania $1.5, Senegal $1.7, Ghana $2.8, Kenya $8.9), though those 12 are only 3.5% of declared value. The band cannot clear the rest: a good used PS5 at $150-200 and ~2.3kg lands at $65-87/kg, inside the band. APPLIED TO THE HARDWARE LEG ONLY - see the Rest of Africa sheet.
